_comment: Every scheduled run writes one record here — including, especially, a run that could not connect. A failed run that logs is data; a failed run that stays silent is a hole in the record, and a hole is indistinguishable from a run that never fired. Record shape: { date, slot: open|hourly|preclose|retro, at, fired, connected, actions, note }. 'connected' means the brokerage connector attached and the run read live account state; a run that reasoned only from this repo's JSON is fired=true, connected=false. Per-run rows begin on recordsBeginOn. Anything earlier is carried in priorSummary as an aggregate, because those runs predate this file and the per-run detail was never written down. Do not backfill it.

scheduler.note: True as of 2026-08-05: a scheduled run has now fired and recorded its own row. Read it narrowly. This is a desktop scheduled task, not a server-side runner — it fires only while the operator's Claude app is open, so a missed window runs late on next launch rather than on time, and the first row here is itself an example: the retro slot is 16:30 ET and it fired at 00:45 ET. Every run therefore checks how late it fired and refuses to write an order specification if the quotes it would rest on are stale. 'Configured' means a trigger exists and has fired, not that the four slots fire reliably at their stated times.

slots.name: Market open
slots.does: Verify the connector attached before reasoning about anything. Check settled cash, apply exit rules, run the six-item pre-trade checklist.

slots.name: Mid-session
slots.does: Enforce exits the hour a level is hit. Default is no trade.

slots.name: Pre-close
slots.does: Exit discipline. Decide overnight holds explicitly rather than by default. Close option no-fly windows.

slots.name: Retro
slots.does: Read-only. Grades the day against the rules outcome-blind, then runs the standing rule-drift check. Never places an order.

_rowFields: trigger: 'scheduled' when the scheduler fired this run in its own window, 'manual' when a human invoked it. Only scheduled rows count toward run health - a manual invocation proves the code path works, not that the system runs. declined: true when the run deliberately stopped on a guard (fired outside its window, or the mandate was unset) and therefore never attempted to reach the broker. A decline is correct behaviour, not a connection failure, and it is excluded from the run-health denominator rather than counted against it.
